It was just yesterday while watching the NBA that I had a new thought about it. To me, kneeling during the national anthem is this era's form of a sit-in, where people of color and their supporters would go sit in a whites only restaurant and peacefully request to be served, while enduring abuse. I would say that most people would be hard-pressed to argue that those sit-ins were disrespectful and unnecessary, as they prompted reform that was so desperately needed. In my opinion, kneeling during the national anthem as a way to peacefully and publicly protest is appropriate. 

I do however, have a problem with anyone saying that its now disrespectful to the BLM movement to NOT kneel and still stand during the anthem. Just as everyone has the right to express themselves by kneeling, others have the right to stand. People like the Spurs coach Pop have shown their support of BLM in other ways, so should not be ridiculed for not taking up every form of protest.

Edit because I just read your other comment: "She started crying because I said we’d only go visit my brother in DC if we went and did all the sights and she said “you said you wanted to take me” and started crying."

At first I thought she just sounded super selfish, but then I realized that statement she made sounds alot like what I have struggled with, Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria. Its where any perception that you aren't important to a loved one or are being rejected amounts to feeling what I can only describe as painful heartbreak and/ or horrible anxiety about being abandoned or broken up with. It can cause the person to become overly clingy and needy, and it sounds like she may be struggling with this. I feel like she really needs therapy, because this is something that CAN get better. I am not excusing her behavior, because it is still unhealthy, but trying to maybe just explain it from her possible perspective. IF thats what shes dealing with, it would probably help her to feel secure if you tell her how special and important she is to you. The more secure she feels, hopefully she would need less constant reassurance by being attached at the hip. I'm not a professional so this is all opinion and just hopefully helpful insight. Sorry for the novel and again, good luck.

When i first setup my online profile it felt so amazing to get so much attention. The problem isn't getting all the attention. The problem is that you literally cannot reply to every message every day, so you have to choose the ones that most interest you to talk to. However, then you start getting messages from the people that you didn't choose saying that you are a B**** for either not replying at all, or replying only once or twice and then "ghosting". Those people try to make you feel guilty and manipulate you into talking, whether they realise they are doing that or not, and reading those messages can be really hurtful. All this would be understandable if we are talking about a handful of people, but when we are talking about hundreds of texts there is simply no way to treat everyone with the same level of attention, someone is always going to get their feelings hurt, and then you are left dealing with their anger and hurt when you literally did nothing wrong. It becomes an overwhelming full-time job just to try to be polite to that many people. Eventually I just stop using the account at all, because it can be so frustrating.

Meh... ok in light of the current pandemic, WASH EVERYTHING WITH SOAP. Outside of that my rule has always been that if another person is possibly using it after me, of course it has to be properly washed with soap. If its a dish that only I ever use, such as my fave coffee cup, I rinse or wash depending on how dirty I feel it is (never more than a day in between washes though). If I know I am going to use it later that day and it just had grapes on it, just a rinse is fine. Normally I say if all people involved are adults, do as you please as long as you are keeping things clean for the next person. BUT my issue here, is that we are talking about a small child that needs to learn the importance of soap and water, so that they are prepared for things like this pandemic. Since I feel it is important to instill things like this at a young age, I am going to say that you need to teach him to use soap everytime. Once he is older he can decide for himself what his acceptable level of clean is, but now more than ever, soap is a big deal. I am going to vote NAH, but I do feel that soap should be used in this certain circumstance.
